1970905901/Y-Player.description: YPlayer - Swift media shell for Apple platforms (iOS/iPadOS + macOS)
1970905901/Y-Player.body:
# YPlayer

An **Apple-platform media shell** built on the [FongMi/TV](https://github.com/FongMi/TV) / [CatVod](https://github.com/FongMi/CatVodSpider) ecosystem. Implemented in Swift, for iOS/iPadOS 15+ and macOS 13+.

Reference implementation: [Silent1566/webhtv](https://github.com/Silent1566/webhtv) (used as the compatibility baseline for protocol and interaction; its Java/Android implementation is not ported).

**Current version: v1.0.3** — download from [Releases](https://github.com/1970905901/Y-Player/releases). For this version's contents and known limitations, see [`docs/发布说明.md`](https://github.com/1970905901/Y-Player/blob/HEAD/docs/发布说明.md).

## Core capabilities

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **.js / .js.md5 interfaces** | **Primary and natively supported**: supports JS sources in the `index.js.md5` and `index.js` forms (with token/version parameters such as `?v=3`; case-insensitive; md5sum text and JSON both accepted). Fully automatic: download → MD5 incremental cache verification → fast startup with embedded Node/JS runtime → local HTTP route dispatch. |
| Playback engine | In-house `PlayerEngine` abstraction; all three engines are **available** and can be selected manually in settings: `system` (AVPlayer, best compatibility), `mpv` (libmpv + MoltenVK, broadest format and multi-audio-track/subtitle coverage), `ffmpeg` (in-house FFmpeg; hardware/software decoding selectable manually, HDR uses hardware decoding; frame-by-frame stepping, gain, and playback info are provided by it). **No automatic fallback at runtime.** |
| Interaction and playback experience | Gesture seek protection while duration is not yet ready; seamless sync of progress when switching lines/episodes; instant re-rendering for multiple subtitle tracks; unique-ID duplicate protection for the aggregated search poster wall. |
| Network and extensions | `headers`/`hosts`/`doh`/`proxy`/`ads`/`hlsRules`/`rules` sniffing rules and a local proxy service; retains `type 0/1/2/4` CMS site protocol decoding compatibility. |
| Unsupported forms | `csp_*.jar` (requires JVM), `.py` (requires CPython), Widevine/PlayReady; the UI explicitly states the reason. |

## Directory structure

```
Apps/                 iOS / macOS app entry points (entry points, Resources, Assets only)
Packages/…
```

AllogeneSSRD/ECM-ELF.description: Multi-backend ECM stage-1 & satge-2 engine (OpenCL · CUDA/CGBN · AVX-512 IFMA) with GMP-ECM & Prime95 savefile interop and a worktodo queue manager. Windows, Linux & Android
AllogeneSSRD/ECM-ELF.body:
# ECM-ELF

[English](https://github.com/AllogeneSSRD/ECM-ELF/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Chinese

ECM-ELF is an elliptic curve factorization (ECM) toolkit: CUDA/CGBN and OpenCL GPU Stage1, GMP and optional AVX-512 IFMA CPU Stage1, a standalone CUDA polynomial Stage2, plus a Windows GUI, task queue, and factor data tools. The original repository name, OpenCL-ECM, covered only one of these backends; the program names remain `ecm.exe`, `ecm_cuda.exe`, and so on.

This page describes the actual purpose of each entry point, runnable commands, configuration methods, save-file relationships, build instructions, and a tool index. For default values, ranges, and bilingual descriptions of configuration keys, the generated [INI reference](https://github.com/AllogeneSSRD/ECM-ELF/blob/HEAD/docs/ECM_INI_REFERENCE.md) is authoritative. Whether a particular build includes a given kernel tier or experimental algorithm should be checked against that program's build identity and help output.

## Compared with mainstream tools

ECM-ELF provides a standalone, multi-backend ECM workflow: batch Stage1 execution using CUDA/CGBN, OpenCL, or CPU, followed by this repository's CUDA polynomial Stage2, or by a qualifying external tool that continues processing completed saves.

- **Compute paths:** CUDA and OpenCL cover different GPU platforms; the CPU path provides GMP scalar and AVX-512 IFMA batch implementations. All paths share the Stage1 task entry point. The actual usable bit widths and algorithms depend on the build version.
- **Standalone Stage2:** CUDA Stage2 uses exact integer polynomial arithmetic and supports direct save reading, an independent queue, per-curve resumption, and parameter tuning and Auto B2 based on measured data. [Stage2 usage](https://github.com/AllogeneSSRD/ECM-ELF/blob/HEAD/docs/usage/STAGE2.md) lists inputs and resource limits.
- **Long-running task management:** worktodo, worker, the Windows GUI, and Prime95 handoff support batch jobs. Stage1 writes checkpoints at safe boundaries and rotates backups; Stage2 uses completion receipts to restore queue progress. [Queues and handoff](#queues) explains the role of each file.
- **Save-file interoperability:** qualifying Suyama PARAM0 and batch PARAM3 saves can be handed to GMP-ECM or Prime95.

BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web.body:
# magpie-gemini-web

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/BUKOWSKIREAL/magpie-gemini-web/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

Use Gemini Web through your Google account in [Magpie](https://usemagpie.ai/). The plugin runs the [gemini-web2api-go](https://github.com/zexadev/gemini-web2api-go) backend locally, converting Gemini Web into an OpenAI-compatible API.

> **2026-10-16 update**: Google AI Pro subscribers who pay full price can now use `gemini-4-argon` directly in Antigravity. Similarly, you can use it directly through the Magpie reverse proxy.

## Getting started

1. Install **magpie-gemini-web** from the Magpie plugin marketplace.
2. Sign in to Gemini Web and select **"One-click configure local Gemini Web (recommended)"**. The plugin automatically downloads the optimized backend published by this project, verifies its SHA-256, and starts it in the background. You don't need to install Go or apply patches manually.
3. Copy the cookie as prompted. **Be sure to use an incognito / private window** (Firefox recommended):
   1. Open <https://gemini.google.com/app> in an incognito window and sign in with the Google account you want to use;
   2. Press F12 (⌥⌘I on macOS), switch to **Network**, and refresh the page;
   3. Click any `gemini.google.com` request → **Headers** → **Request Headers**;
   4. Copy the value of the `cookie` line and paste it back into Magpie;
   5. Close the incognito window directly. **Do not click sign out**, because signing out will invalidate this cookie.
4. The plugin automatically completes sign-in once it detects that the account is usable.

> **Why use an incognito window?** The backend periodically refreshes this login to keep it alive. If it shares the same login session as the browser you normally use, Google will invalidate the session and your browser will sign out of all Google services. An incognito window gives the backend its own separate session. The safer approach is to use a separate Google secondary account for the backend.

After this, Magpie automatically starts the backend every time it launches, so you don't need to manage it. To add more accounts, just run the one-click configuration again.

> Need a proxy to access Google? The backend does not read `HTTP_PROXY`. Add one in the proxy pool on the admin panel at `http://127.0.0.1:8083/admin`. The login token is the `adminToken` value in the data directory's `secrets.json`. …

# [Kingdom Study Session] NIKKE Tactical Preparation Room

NIKKE Workshop is a local extension for Chromium browsers. It integrates account character data retrieval, Nikke encyclopedia and list management, equipment affix reading, a finite-state MDP calculator for affix rerolling, and Excel export.

Current version: `1.0.15`　|　Supports: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge

1.0.15 keeps the whole-task Web Worker and optimizes reroll-affix solving, probability transition reuse, and global candidate computation. The default is the “old rules,” and you can switch to the “new rules.” After a sync failure, the normal retry wait is shortened to 10 seconds. The 60-second cooldown after a successful sync and the server-side rate-limit protection are unchanged. This release also ships the previously accepted new characters, skins, and local avatars. Performance samples and validation boundaries are in [Calculation Optimization Validation](https://github.com/ChrisLu7899/NIKKE-Workshop/blob/HEAD/docs/计算优化验证-20261016.md).

The current client static value package is still pending compatibility with the parsing configuration. This release did not modify probabilities based on the old package, and it does not claim the new values are verified. Asset coverage was cross-checked against both the previously accepted official online character list and the character table from the most recent successful unpacking.

1.0.14 added the accepted Gilti: Divine Rabbit Girl and Mori: Swift Rabbit Girl with default full-body portraits. Before the installer package was generated, each default portrait mapping, source, and file hash was checked one by one against the new character table, so that the version number was not updated while new character assets were missed.

2026-09-16 recommendation revision: based on the user-reviewed one-image guide, 87 training recommendations were updated. The water-cooled main carry “布丽德” was corrected to “布蕾德” (Bulede), with the synced skill plus signs, red tier, and conditional notes updated to match. It remains 1.0.11. Users who already installed this version should download the new full package, overwrite the old one, and reload the extension. The same version number will not trigger an automatic update prompt. See [One-Image Guide Review Record](https://github.com/ChrisLu7899/NIKKE-Workshop/blob/HEAD/docs/一图流复核-20260916.md).

Installation and updates use `NIKKE-Workshop.zip` uniformly. It includes all 625 portraits, so no separate asset download or asset download permission is needed. Character cards read images directly from the installation directory. See [Full Installer Package Notes](https://github.com/ChrisLu7899/NIKKE-Workshop/blob/HEAD/docs/完整安装包交付.md).

1.0.11: After you click “版本更新” (Version Update) at the bottom of the sidebar, the latest version is queried automatically. The plugin update window keeps only the “关闭” (Close) and “打开更新器” (Open Updater) buttons. The Windows updater supports “选择目录” (Select Directory). You can switch to another complete plugin installation folder, and the version in that folder is read automatically and must be reconfirmed. KannaKuron/dsh-ide-git.body:
# dsh-ide-git

Simplified Chinese | [English](https://github.com/KannaKuron/dsh-ide-git/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md)

> Adds an **IDE-grade Git tool window** to the sidebar of [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): a branch tree on the left, a commit graph in the middle, and changes and commit details on the right. Operations are aligned with the Git panels of JetBrains IDEs. It is registered as a native tab of [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) and works in both the right sidebar and the bottom panel. Since v0.13.0 it can also be mounted in the **main conversation area** (a Git tab next to "Conversation / Trace", which can be turned off in settings).

DSH's built-in Git panel covers "stage / commit / restore / view history". `dsh-ide-git` adds the layer that IDE users expect: **branch tree + right-click branch actions + commit graph + commit details + changes list + commit box**.

## What it solves

- **Branch management has no tree**: the built-in panel has only a branch dropdown. Here you get a grouped tree of `HEAD (current branch) / Local / Remote / Tags`, where each branch shows ahead/behind badges, its upstream, and a worktree occupancy marker (`W`).
- **History is just a list**: here the commit graph is drawn (lane topology plus branch/tag ref badges), with load-more and filtering by text, hash, or author.
- **Want to see what a commit changed**: click a commit to open its details: author, date, full commit message, and changed files with +/− line counts. Click a file to see a line-by-line diff (red/green, line numbers, and hunk highlighting).
- **Want to point the AI at a piece of code**: in the diff view, select a few lines and right-click to send "which file, which lines" (with commit or working-tree context) straight to the input box of the current session.
- **Want to compare branches**: right-click a branch to compare it with the current branch. Results are reported by file and commit count.
- **Complete set of operations**: checkout, create a branch from any branch or commit, rename, delete, merge into current, rebase current onto here, create a tag, cherry-pick, revert a commit, reset (keep/discard), and fetch / pull --ff-only / push (after confirmation).

## iOS App Maintenance

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 16.19.1
MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
npx cap sync ios
npx cap open ios
```

Then select iPhone in Xcode and press `Cmd + R` to install.

NoNameLeGo/torrent-search-app.body:
# BT Aggregated Search · Torrent Meta-Search

A desktop-oriented **BT torrent aggregation search engine**. Enter a keyword and **40+ torrent sites** are searched in parallel. Results stream in in real time via SSE and are deduplicated across sites and merged into a single card. It relies on no third-party services and runs entirely locally.

> ⚠️ **This project was generated with AI assistance**. It draws on the parallel multi-engine aggregation approach of [prajwalch/TorrentSearch](https://github.com/prajwalch/TorrentSearch) (a native Kotlin/Android app) and was rewritten as a Node/Express backend, vanilla JS frontend, and Electron desktop shell. The code may be studied, modified, and redistributed, but **completeness and security are not guaranteed**. Please review it yourself before use.

> 🦀 **Development status (updated 2026-10-16): The Rust rewrite has completed M0–M7, and `main` is now the Rust mainline.**
> **[`v0.3.6-beta`](https://github.com/NoNameLeGo/torrent-search-app/releases) has been released.** The artifacts include
> **a single-file Rust exe: 18 MB, zero runtime dependencies** (no Node, no WebView2, no VC++ runtime needed).
> The old Node/Express + Electron/Tauri variants **continue to be provided in the same Release**, and the Node version is archived at `legacy/node-electron`.
> ⚠️ **The Rust version currently has only 16 engines** (the Node version has 40), no Torznab support, and downloader settings are not persisted ⇒
> **Suitable for early adopters, not yet for daily primary use.** For guidance on which to choose, see [`docs/RELEASE_ARTIFACTS.md`](https://github.com/NoNameLeGo/torrent-search-app/blob/HEAD/docs/RELEASE_ARTIFACTS.md).
> - **End goal**: a native Windows desktop app: single file, zero runtime dependencies, fast startup, low memory. The browser / mobile access mode has been abandoned.
> - **Path (re-planned 2026-10-11)**: **go directly to a native Slint UI**, with the core built as a **library** (called in-process, no HTTP, no SSE).
>   The earlier plan of 'Phase 1 = reuse the WebView frontend' has been **retired**, because it could not produce a 'small, fast, native' product. See [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/NoNameLeGo/torrent-search-app/blob/HEAD/docs/ROADMAP.md) for details.

## What this repository does

2. **Keeps only Agent Benchmarks**: first retrieves candidates with queries related to agent + benchmark, then filters them with keyword scoring (LLM agent, web/GUI/coding agent, tool-use, computer-use, etc.). Excludes ordinary RL agents, reagents / pathogens, and other unrelated uses.

bennytsai1234/Night-Reader.body:
A novel reader for Android built for long-form fiction: your own book sources, your own typesetting, and readable even offline.

---

Night Reader searches, reads, and downloads web novels from the book sources you import, and can also read local TXT files. Its book source rules are compatible with [Legado (閱讀)](https://github.com/gedoor/legado), reimplemented in Flutter. The app does not bundle any book sources or novel content.

## Features

- **Comfortable typesetting**: Font size, line height, letter spacing, paragraph spacing, and indentation are all adjustable, and Chinese punctuation and mixed Chinese-English text are neatly aligned. There are ten styles (Paper Ink, Bamboo Green, Azurite Blue, Tea Brown, Plain, Rouge, Lotus, Yellow Scroll, Amber, and Frost Night), each paired with light, dark, or system-following modes. The accent color for switches and buttons can also be chosen separately.
- **Automatic offline bookshelf**: Books added to the shelf are automatically downloaded in full, new chapters are fetched when they appear, and books remain readable without a network connection.
- **Search all sources at once**: Multiple book sources are searched simultaneously, Traditional and Simplified Chinese are searched together, and the same book is merged into a single entry. You can also browse book sources by their 'Discover' categories.
- **Switch sources without losing your place**: After switching to another book source, your reading progress stays on the same chapter.
- **Audiobooks**: Text is read aloud using the Android system's speech engine, with adjustable speed and pitch, a sleep timer for pausing, and highlighting of the sentence currently being read.
- **Text cleanup**: Replacement rules remove ads and noise, and convert between Traditional and Simplified Chinese.
- **Book source tools**: Batch validation finds broken book sources, and a single source can be debugged step by step across search, details, table of contents, and body text.
- **Portable data**: The bookshelf, book sources, replacement rules, and settings can be backed up and restored (original local TXT files must be saved separately). You can also import and export the bookshelf, and export whole books as TXT.

## Download and Updates

Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/bennytsai1234/night-reader/releases). It supports Android arm64 devices.

The app checks for new versions when it opens. When connected to Wi-Fi, it downloads updates in the background first, then prompts you to install. To try new features early, turn on 'Receive beta updates' under 'Me' → 'About Night Reader'. Changes in each version are listed under 'Changelog' or in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/bennytsai1234/Night-Reader/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md).

The same Release also includes unsigned iOS installers (`.ipa`). You need to sign and install these yourself with AltStore or Sideloadly using an Apple ID (free accounts must re-sign every 7 days). The iOS version has no in-app updates, no sharing into the app, and no opening books from files. It has not been tested on an actual iPhone.

## Getting Started

1. After installing, go to 'Me' → 'Book Source Management' and import your own book sources (from a URL, file, or clipboard).
2. Find books through search or Discover, and add them to your bookshelf.
3. Books on the shelf download automatically and remain readable offline.

When first installed, the bookshelf and search are empty, because Night Reader does not include any book sources.

# BTIR Brain Tumor MRI Image Analysis Platform

BTIR is a complete analysis system for four-modality brain tumor MRI. Users can log in through the browser, complete classification, segmentation, and AI-assisted analysis, and view key imaging features, slices, comparisons, and 3D images on the web page.

You can self-host the server and use the matching client project: https://github.com/ckckh2023/BTIR-Client

Access our already-deployed service (opened irregularly): https://btir-online.ai-premol.cn

You can also visit our about page: https://btir.xiao-blog.top/

**Other languages:** [English](https://github.com/ckckh2023/BTIR-BrainTumor-ImageRecognition/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

## Project Capabilities

| Scope | Capability |
| --- | --- |
| Case upload | Supports four-modality NIfTI or raw DICOM folders and ZIP files, automatically matches and converts FLAIR, T1CE, T1, and T2; when NIfTI files are missing or duplicated, provides corresponding correction options |
| Model analysis | Local ViT multi-slice binary classification and SuperLightNet 3D segmentation jointly provide evidence and generate a comprehensive conclusion |
| Results display | The first screen shows the combined conclusion of both models, follow-up comparison, and key imaging features; below it, slice probability curves, segmentation overlays, and on-demand expandable regional details are provided |
| 3D viewing | Switch between four modalities, three views, and volume rendering; overlay predicted masks and adjust opacity |
| Follow-up and tasks | Group historical exams by case and select two results to compare; supports asynchronous submission, progress polling, cancellation, retry after failure, run history, archiving, and restore |
| Multi-user | JWT login isolation, per-user task quotas, forced password change, administrator user and task management, audit queries |
| Test assurance | Unit tests, interface contracts, task workflow tests, and optional browser end-to-end tests |
| Deployment and runtime | SQLite persistence, Redis + RQ queue, CPU, CUDA, and Linux ROCm runtime support; audit logs rotated by size and automatically retained |

# JumpServer Installer

JumpServer Installer is used to install and manage JumpServer.

## Environment Requirements
  - Linux x86_64
  - Kernel greater than 4.0

## Docker / Compose Download and OSS Sync

Binary download addresses are defined directly in `scripts/const.sh`. Setting the environment variable `DOCKER_IMAGE_MIRROR=1` switches the download domain for Docker and Compose to `https://download.jumpserver.org`; when this switch is not enabled, you can specify another download domain via the environment variable `DOCKER_BIN_HOST`. The installer always verifies downloaded content using the SHA-256 values fixed in `scripts/const.sh`.

The GitHub Actions workflow **Sync Docker Binaries to OSS** automatically reads the version number from this file and the SHA-256 values for both architectures (`x86_64`, `aarch64`), downloads all files from the official source and verifies them, then uploads the binaries along with the `.sha256` and `.md5` files to the `jms-pkg` bucket in the Beijing region. Object paths keep the part of the official URL after removing the domain:

```text
oss://jms-pkg/linux/static/stable/<arch>/docker-<version>.tgz
oss://jms-pkg/docker/compose/releases/download/<version>/docker-compose-linux-<arch>
```

Add the following in the installer repository under **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**:

- `OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
- `OSS_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET`

Credentials are passed in via ossutil environment variables and are not written to the repository or configuration files. The RAM authorization scope should cover the object write and upload permissions required for `jms-pkg/linux/static/stable/*` and `jms-pkg/docker/compose/releases/download/*`.

Synchronization runs automatically when changes to version configuration, sync scripts, or the workflow are pushed to the `dev`, `master`, `main`, or `v*` branches. You can also manually **Run workflow** from the Actions page to sync the versions declared on the selected branch. When upgrading versions, both architectures' SHA-256 values must be updated together; no workflow changes are needed. Uploads are performed file by file, and historical versions or other objects in the bucket are not deleted.

River Review is an OSS framework that treats review standards as **versioned / repo-owned skills**. It can run across SDLC artifacts such as plan / diff / tests / JUnit / existing review results. It currently provides the **Review Judgment Platform**, a team-owned audit layer for operating your team's review judgment. For an overview of the concept, see [Concept](https://river-review.the3396.com/explanation/concept/).

AI-assisted development (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor, etc.) has made writing code much faster. However, **review judgment remains the team's responsibility**, and it must stay explicit, reproducible, and owned by the team.

River Review is a framework for answering questions like these:

- Does this diff match the approved implementation plan?
- Do the tests meet the boundary conditions promised in the plan?
- Does this PR violate the team's migration / security / a11y / dependency policies?
- Is the implementation agent ignoring feedback from past reviews?

> River Review does not replace human review with AI. By running the team's judgment criteria as versioned skills, it lets humans focus on the high-risk judgments that truly need them ([Human Judgment Focus](https://river-review.the3396.com/explanation/human-judgment-focus/)).

workdd/I_AM_ML_Engineer.body:
# I AM ML Engineer

A repository that digs into what you've read down to "why it was built this way"

**Full-text search** · **Topic-based table of contents** · **Diagram rendering** · **Automatic following of the system theme**

It reads just as well on a phone.

## About

I read and summarize papers, technical blogs, and open-source repositories. The goal is not summaries but notes in a **form you can use for decisions**.

Each write-up follows these principles:

- **Check the original**: Figures and quotations are verified directly against the original source. Secondhand material is not copied over
- **State limitations**: Note the conditions under which results were obtained and how far they generalize
- **Cross-link**: Materials addressing the same problem are linked to each other
- **Points of application**: Principles from what I read that can be transferred elsewhere are extracted separately

y50008/docker-pack.body:
# 🐳 Docker Pack GUI

**A visual tool that packages project source code into Docker images with one click. Double-click to run, no dependencies to install.**

Author: y50008 ｜ Open-source repository: https://github.com/y50008/docker-pack

---

## 📖 Project Overview

Docker Pack GUI is a **Windows desktop** tool for packaging Docker images. **Download the exe and double-click to open it. You don't need to install Python or configure any environment**, because the tool bundles all runtime files into the exe.

Just select a project source directory (or enter a Git repository URL), click "Start Packaging", and the tool will automatically:

1. **Detect the project language/framework** (supports 23 types, see below)
2. **Automatically generate a multi-stage Dockerfile** (China-based mirror sources for faster downloads, dependency cache reuse)
3. **Call Docker to build the image** (single-architecture or multi-architecture, with real-time BuildKit progress parsing)
4. **Export as a `.tar` (or `.tar.gz`) file** for you to download and save
5. **Optional**: post-build self-check, one-click generation of docker-compose.yml, and pushing to an image registry

> No need to write a Dockerfile by hand or memorize `docker build` commands. Even beginners can produce production-grade images.

### ✨ What's New in v1.4

- **Cancel builds at any time**: during a build, click "Cancel Build" to immediately terminate the build process instead of having to close the program
- **Log in to image registries**: run `docker login` directly in the interface without switching to the command line
- **Git branches/tags**: specify a branch or tag when cloning a repository
- **Monorepo subdirectories**: build only a specified subdirectory of a repository
- **Build argument injection**: enter one `KEY=VALUE` per line, automatically passed to `docker build --build-arg`
- **Export compression**: one-click compression to `.tar.gz` for a smaller size and easier transfer
- **Configurable output directory with automatic cleanup**: choose where artifacts are saved; by default only the 20 most recent archives are kept
- **Custom Dockerfile templates**: override the built-in templates with `templates/<type>.dockerfile` or the `DOCKER_PACK_TEMPLATES` environment variable
- **Input validation and localized error messages**: image names, tags, and ports are validated instantly; common English errors such as the daemon not running, insufficient disk space, port conflicts, and network timeouts are automatically translated into Chinese hints, and a Docker environment check runs before building
- **Web version security hardening**: access token authentication, server path allowlist, zip upload extraction, feature parity with the desktop version, and a built-in production-grade WSGI server (waitress)
